Hi Sara / Brian —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Per our discussion, HealthCore wants a short pilot (6 weeks) that requires:
- a contractual no-training / no-model-improvement commitment for the data sent during the pilot,
- customer ownership of prompts and model outputs, and
- a limited SLA exception (higher availability targets and credit terms) for the pilot window.

Attached are two artifacts to start the review:
- HealthCore-DPA-draft.pdf (redline from procurement) [attachment stub]
- SLA-exception-redline.docx (our proposed exception language) [attachment stub]

High-level answers we can confirm up-front:
- Operationally we can enforce a tenant-level "no-improve" toggle (platform flag) so data is not used for model improvement. We will log the flag and provide an attestation.
- Outputs (generated text) and prompts are covered by our standard output license to customers; we'll reflect that explicitly in the DPA addendum.
- Subprocessors: we will provide a current inventory and SOC2 / SCCs and are open to a short attestation packet for the pilot.

Open items where we need HealthCore input: scope of the pilot data (PHI subsets?), residency/KMS preferences, and whether HealthCore requires an onshore-only KMS for the pilot.

Next steps I propose:
1) HealthCore legal to propose redlines on the DPA (we can intake via DocuSign link).
2) Redwood legal (Kimberly) to review SLA exception redline and sign off on scope.
3) Operations to enable no-improve toggle for the tenant and provide an evidence snapshot.

If you want, we can schedule a 30-min call to walk legal/procurement through the operational guarantees.

Thanks,

David —

Thanks for the quick follow-up and attachments. A few clarifying questions from HealthCore legal/procurement before we loop any redlines: 

1) Scope: The pilot will include PII and limited PHI (hashed IDs + notes). We need to confirm the no-train toggle covers all data planes (streaming + logs + telemetry).

2) Subprocessors: Please provide current subprocessor list and whether any third-party inference or logging vendors see raw prompts or outputs.

3) KMS & residency: For compliance we need an onshore KMS for key material used to encrypt stored logs during the pilot; can Redwood commit to US-residency for that KMS?

4) Prompt/output ownership: We need explicit language that HealthCore maintains exclusive rights to prompts and generated outputs for our customer data during the pilot and that Redwood will not assert derivative/model rights.

Procurement asked for an estimated timeline to finalize these two docs (DPA + SLA exception). Ideally we'd like contract sign-off within 10 business days to keep the pilot schedule.

If helpful, we can do a short call tomorrow afternoon to walk through requirements.

Best,

Sara / Brian —

Appreciate the detailed asks. Below are direct responses and the operational guardrails we can provide for the pilot. I'll flag legal items for Kimberly to formalize in contract language.

Operational commitments (we can deliver these for the pilot):
- No-train toggle: We will enable a tenant-level "no_improve" flag covering model training and offline pipelines. This prevents any of the pilot traffic from entering retraining datasets or aggregator telemetry used for model updates. We will capture an immutable audit snapshot at toggle-on and share the snapshot (hash + timestamp).
- Data planes: The toggle applies to request bodies (prompts), intermediate KV caches, and any async logging. We will ensure sampling is disabled for the tenant for pilot duration.
- Subprocessors: Current subprocessor list will be attached separately to the DocuSign intake; short answer: our inference runtime and S3-compatible storage vendors will process data, and logging is routed to our internal platform (no third-party analytics vendors by default). We can provide SOC2 reports and a subprocessor attestation.
- KMS/residency: We can provision a US-resident customer-managed KMS for the pilot (AWS KMS key in US region) and restrict export by policy. Ops needs a 3-business-day lead to wire the key and test.
- Prompt/output ownership: Redwood will accept explicit DPA language: Customer retains ownership and exclusive rights to prompts and generated outputs for their tenant. Redwood will not claim derivative/model rights over pilot data.
- SLA exception: Proposed pilot SLA: 99.9% monthly uptime, with service credits for breaches and a 24/7 on-call escalation path. See SLA-exception-redline.docx [attachment].

Next steps:
- HealthCore to provide any redlines to the DPA (DocuSign link included).
- I will ask Kimberly to propose tight contract language implementing the points above and confirm KMS routing.
- Ops (Marissa) will prepare the evidence snapshot and subprocessor attestation.

Target timeline if we proceed immediately: 7–10 business days to sign DPA + SLA exception and provision KMS.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call to walk the legal/ops teams through the evidence artifacts.

-David

Kimberly's legal notes (high level):
- The proposed no-train language is acceptable but we should add a defined-term "No-Model-Improvement Period" with explicit start/end dates for the pilot to avoid ambiguity.
- Add a representation that Redwood will not use any aggregated anonymous telemetry derived from pilot data for model updates during a 12-month restricted period. (Client asked for pilot-only; legal prefers a 12-month contractual backstop.)
- KMS: we can provision US-residency key material but procurement must own the key (customer-managed) or we need a certified escrow process. Recommend customer-managed KMS for simplicity.
- Subprocessor attestation: require a dated attestation (PDF) listing subprocessor access scopes and a contact for audit questions.
- Prompt/output ownership: contract language should explicitly prohibit Redwood from claiming derivative IP and require Redwood to delete any ephemeral copies used only for routing within X hours unless otherwise logged and agreed.

1) David / Marissa: prepare the operational attestation packet and an evidence snapshot (audit logs + toggle timestamp).
